newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-NEBIOLO SAYS JAPAN, KOREA SUPPORT ROME BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-NEBIOLO SAYS JAPAN, KOREA SUPPORT ROME BID.

text.p: International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) president Primo Nebiolo said on Saturday that Japan and South Korea supported Rome's bid to host the 2004 Summer Olympics.
"I have returned from Korea with optimism about Rome's candidature to host the 2004 Olympics," said Nebiolo, an Italian and one of the most influential figures in world sport.

"During the winter University Games I met various personalities in the Japanese and South Korean world of sports, industry and politics -- many of whom are involved in the Olympics -- and all favoured Rome's candidature," he said.
"Asia doesn't have any cities as candidates and so it is open to calm, impartial and reasonable evaluations."
The IOC will announce a shortlist of four candidates in March from the current 11 cities bidding to host the 2004 Games. The winning city will be named in September.
The 11 candidates are Rome, St Petersburg, Cape Town, Stockholm, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Buenos Aires, Athens, Lille, Seville and Istanbul.
